title: Similar String Groups
statement: Call two strings *similar* when they are equal, or when exchanging the characters at two different positions of one of them produces the other. Similarity links the words of `strs` into groups: two words share a group whenever a chain of similar words connects them, even if the two are not similar to each other directly. Every word in `strs` is an anagram of every other word (same length, same letters). Return the number of groups.
constraints: strs[i] contains only lowercase English letters
All words have the same length and are anagrams of each other
notes:
## Intuition

Treat each word as a node and join two nodes with an edge when the words are similar. The answer is the number of connected components. Because all words are anagrams, two words are similar exactly when they differ in 0 or 2 positions (they can never differ in just one), so similarity is a cheap position-by-position count. A brute force could try every swap of one word to see if it yields the other, but counting mismatches is far faster.

## Approach

1. Give every index its own set in a union-find: `parent[i] = i`. Start `groups` at `n`.
2. `find` climbs to a set's root, halving the path as it goes.
3. `similar` counts mismatched positions and gives up as soon as there are more than 2.
4. For every pair `i < j` of similar words, find both roots. If they differ, link one root under the other and decrease `groups`.
5. Return `groups`.

## Example 1, step by step

`strs = ["tars", "rats", "arts", "star"]`, so `groups` starts at 4.

- `tars`/`rats` differ at positions 0 and 2: similar. Roots 0 and 1 merge, `groups = 3`.
- `tars`/`arts` differ in 3 positions, and `star` differs from every word in 4: not similar.
- `rats`/`arts` differ at positions 0 and 1: similar. Roots 1 and 2 merge, `groups = 2`.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n² · L): each of the n² / 2 pairs is compared in at most L steps; union-find work is nearly constant.
- Space: O(n) for `parent`.

## Pitfalls

- Groups are connected components, not cliques: `tars` and `arts` share a group through `rats`.
- Identical words (0 mismatches) are similar too, so duplicates join the same group.
- Only decrease `groups` when the two roots differ; otherwise words already linked would be counted twice.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parent` | union-find parent of each word's index |
| `groups` | number of separate sets so far |
| `diff` | mismatched positions between two words |
| `i`, `j` | indices of the pair being compared |
| `rootI`, `rootJ` | set roots of words `i` and `j` |
